#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build and run the bounded P4M frontend/observer integration test.

This is an integration-wiring and edge-accounting check against the real
frontend and the real observer.  The synthetic backends are not an AXI timing
model; no FPGA, datapath throughput or continuous-performance claim is made.
Verilator build output is kept on disk only when the build fails.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
cva6 = root / 'cva6'
out = root / 'out/p4m-baseline-20260920/pair'
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

base = 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/frontends/register_64bit/idma_reg64_frontend.sv'
prim = cva6 / 'core_apu/register_interface/vendor/lowrisc_opentitan/src'
files = [
    cva6 / 'vendor/pulp-platform/common_cells/include/common_cells/registers.svh',
    cva6 / 'vendor/pulp-platform/axi/src/axi_pkg.sv',
    cva6 / 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/idma_pkg.sv',
    cva6 / 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/frontends/register_64bit/idma_reg64_frontend_reg_pkg.sv',
    prim / 'prim_subreg_arb.sv', prim / 'prim_subreg.sv', prim / 'prim_subreg_ext.sv',
    cva6 / 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/frontends/register_64bit/idma_reg64_frontend_reg_top.sv',
    cva6 / 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/frontends/idma_transfer_id_gen.sv',
    cva6 / base,
    cva6 / 'corev_apu/fpga/src/dma_observer.sv',
    root / 'tests/idma_p4m_pair_top.sv',
    root / 'tests/idma_p4m_pair_test.cpp',
]

cmd = ['verilator', '--cc', '--exe', '--build', '-Wno-fatal',
       '--top-module', 'idma_p4m_pair_top',
       '--Mdir', str(out),
       '-I' + str(cva6 / 'vendor/pulp-platform/common_cells/include'),
       '-I' + str(cva6 / 'corev_apu/iDMA/src/include')] + list(map(str, files))

build = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
if build.returncode:
    (out / 'build.log').write_text(build.stdout)
    raise SystemExit('verilator build failed; inspect ' + str(out / 'build.log'))

subprocess.run([str(out / 'Vidma_p4m_pair_top')], check=True)

risks: Highest risk: word13 semantics. I implemented `V issued includes first` (task note) plus contract word +13 being the only unqualified `Vissued`/`Vdone` pair, so the oracle counts the opening V issue (word13 == n, word14 == n) while A issue/done sums (words 2/3) exclude the opening edge per the explicitly 'inside window' wording and word7 reporting the opening-edge A issue separately. If Codex's focused observer revision keeps the strict `(open, close]` rule for V as well, the oracle needs exactly one change: move the `if (v_iss) ++v_issued;` line inside the `armed && open && !closed` window guard in tests/idma_p4m_pair_test.cpp and expect word13 == n-1.

The `observer did freeze after the V CPU poll` assertion depends on the observer's poll-ID semantics. Reading the supplied dma_observer.sv: `obs_poll_id_o` returns `batch_completed_q` while `expected_q` is refreshed to the latest victim issue ID (`batch_issued_q + 1`) on every V issue, so at closure both equal n and the freeze should fire; any change to that pairing in the focused revision must keep the equality, otherwise this assertion (not the bank comparison) fails first.

The isolated `p4m_bad_carry_done` fixture assumes the production `idma_p4m_validate` rejects a strict pre-opening cohort whose carried job completion was counted (flags bit2 set, first_done_id == open id, done > 0) while carry_done stays 0. linux/drivers/misc/idma.c was not supplied, so this expectation is inferred from the existing fixture set (p4m_bad_carry asserts carry_done > start is an error; p4m_bad_ids asserts done > 0 requires non-zero IDs). If the validator does not encode this cross-check, the fixture must be dropped rather than the assertion relaxed.

Per integration-task item 3 the observer is under a focused revision (initial V issue plus per-lane tracking). The new integration test therefore encodes corrected behaviour and may legitimately fail against the current tree before that revision lands; this is intended, but it means the new C++ test must not be used as evidence about the unrevised RTL.

The optional pre-ARM warm-up uses a non-batch copy on lane A. Because the observer's A-lane event taps are gated by `has_a_q` (only set at ARM), the warm-up perturbs only the functional ID generators and lane stock, not `a_task_q`/`a_id_q`. If the intent of 'verifies tracking across batch IDs' is deeper (for example a warm-up that must populate the tracked A task before ARM), the harness needs a different stimulus and this must be decided by Codex.

The `a_pages` sweep for the A lane is only exercised in co-run mode, and solo mode is exercised with gap 0 only, because the contract forbids a non-zero V gap for P4M and solo has no A lane. If the intent was to sweep the V lane's own gap in solo mode, that contradicts contract line 6 and needs an explicit decision.
Not executed here: no Verilator build, no host C compilation and no simulation were run. Every PASS/FAIL statement in this proposal is a proposed acceptance check, not an observed result.
